headword: {大盤振|おおばんぶ}る{舞|ま}い

definitions.gloss: lavish spending; generous treat; extravagant hospitality
definitions.explanation: An act of spending generously or treating people lavishly, especially when hosting a feast or giving gifts. Can be positive (genuine generosity) or slightly critical (excessive spending).

examples.japanese: {社長|しゃちょう}の{大盤振|おおばんぶ}る{舞|ま}いで{全員|ぜんいん}{招待|しょうたい}された。
examples.english: Everyone was invited thanks to the president's generous treat.

examples.japanese: ボーナスが{出|で}て、{大盤振|おおばんぶ}る{舞|ま}いの{食事会|しょくじかい}を{開|ひら}いた。
examples.english: After getting my bonus, I threw a lavish dinner party.

examples.japanese: {政府|せいふ}は{選挙前|せんきょまえ}になると{大盤振|おおばんぶ}る{舞|ま}いの{政策|せいさく}を{打|う}ち{出|だ}す{傾向|けいこう}がある。
examples.english: The government tends to announce generous spending policies before elections.

notes:
Originally referred to serving food on a large tray ({大盤|おおばん}) in a grand manner ({振|ふ}る{舞|ま}い, a feast or banquet). Now used more broadly for any lavish or generous spending or entertaining.

USAGE:
Can carry either a positive nuance (admiring someone's generosity) or a slightly negative one (implying reckless or politically motivated spending), depending on context.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {大盤振|おおばんぶ}る{舞|ま}いをする: to spend lavishly, to treat generously
- {大盤振|おおばんぶ}る{舞|ま}いの～: a lavish ~

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {奮発|ふんぱつ}する: to splurge — deciding to spend more than usual on a particular purchase
- {散財|さんざい}する: to spend freely — often implies wasting money
- {気前|きまえ}がいい: generous — a personality trait rather than a specific act
